label: OptiXtrans E9605 OTN platform, DC, 5x TNG1N210 (50x 10G line)
description: Huawei OptiXtrans E9605 - compact optical subrack for OLA and ROADM line-degree sites (177 mm x 442 mm x 260 mm, 7.6 kg, 5 service board slots). Modelled with all five service slots (IU1-IU5) filled by TNG1N210 line boards: 50x 10G OTU2 line ports on SFP+. No client tributary port exists until a tributary board is fitted; the CTU pair in IU73-IU74, the PIU/APIU pair in IU100-IU101 and the EFI boards in IU71-IU72 add no service ports.
notes: Slot map from the E9605 Subrack chapter (117,447 B, 2 pp): "Service board areas | 5 service boards | IU1-IU5", two CTU boards in IU73-IU74, two PIU/APIU boards in IU100-IU101, two EFI boards in IU71-IU72, fan IU90, 177 x 442 x 260 mm, 7.6 kg. The brochure agrees on "Max. number of service board slots: 5". Ports: TNG1N210 is "10 x 10 Gbit/s Line Service Processing Board" in the boards-overview Table 3, so 5 slots x 10 = 50; each port is a 10G optical line (OTU2/OTU2e) interface in an SFP+ cage, the 10G optical module the E9600 family brochure lists among its supported pluggables. The SFP+ cage itself is not printed in any public chapter - the board datasheet that carries the front panel (EDOC1100163901) answers 302 -> /view/notFound - so the cage is derived from the 10G optical line rate, not transcribed. Build provenance. The frame half is vendor-stated: `https://e-file.huawei.com/marketingcloud/pep/asset/20000001/Material/0f9e00e3f2ca431693884a01667d7ec6/M3T1A669N1188254857740624027/OptiXtrans%20E9600%20Family%20-.pdf` (Product Brochure, 277,705 B) prints the "Max. number of service board slots" row, and the subrack chapters print the slot map. The card half is vendor-stated too, but from a partner mirror rather than a Huawei host: `https://www.actfornet.com/solutions/solution/OptiXtrans_E9600_Boards_Overview` (HTTP 200, 226,637 B) reproduces the hedex chapter *OptiXtrans E9600 (E9624/E9612/E9605) Boards Overview* (`EDOC1100126589`) and carries Table 3, "Mapping between the line boards and OptiXtrans 9800 E9624/E9612/E9605 subrack", whose TNG1N206/TNG1N210 row reads E9624 "1:1 mode: Y 1:3 mode: Y", E9612 "Y", E9605 "Y". That is the board-to-subrack validity no Huawei-hosted document publishes (the board chapters answer 302 -> /view/notFound; see research/optixtrans-client-board-chapters.md). The complement is a build recorded here, not a vendor configuration: every service slot is filled with the same line board, the convention devices/huawei/optixtrans-e6616.json and devices/arista/7504r.json already use. A shelf with tributary (TNG1T212/TNG1A212) or WSS boards fitted in some slots is a different box with a different port list.
